name: Deep Research
description: Run an in-depth, multi-source web research project on a question and publish a long cited report to the research site. Use only when the user asks for deep or thorough research, a report, a literature or market review, or a comparison that needs many sources; it takes several minutes. For quick facts or current news, use web search instead.
author: anything

input.hint: Model that plans, checks for gaps, writes and fact-checks: glm-* runs on Z.AI, anything else on DeepSeek.
Model for the parallel search-and-read workers, run with thinking off (so a DeepSeek model: glm-5.3 can't turn thinking off).
DeepSeek model the planner switches to for the rest of a run when Z.AI says the GLM plan's usage is spent (429 or 1113); 'off' lets the run go on without it.
Zola site the reports are published to (section 'reports').

How the research is done: 'pipeline' (our own workers on SearXNG, with the planner and worker models above) or 'agents' (AnythingLLM's own agents in the agents-planner and agents-worker workspaces, through agents-runner; being compared, see README).
Also add each report to the workspace's documents so later chats can search it; 'no' turns this off. Reports are always saved to the agent's files (research/).

examples.prompt: Do deep research on how heat pumps perform in Nordic winters
examples.call: {"question": "How do air-source heat pumps perform in Nordic winters: efficiency at low temperatures, real-world field data, and costs compared with alternatives?", "depth": "standard"}

examples.prompt: Write me a quick research report comparing Zola, Hugo and Eleventy
examples.call: {"question": "How do the static site generators Zola, Hugo and Eleventy compare in features, performance, templating and ecosystem?", "depth": "quick"}

question.description: The full research question, self-contained and specific: include the scope, time frame and what to compare, since the researchers can't see the chat.

depth.description: How deep to go: "quick" (a few minutes), "standard" (default, about 5-10 minutes) or "thorough" (10-20 minutes, only when the user asks for thorough or exhaustive research). Use quick only when the user asks for something fast.
